title: Folionaire - portfolio tracker (ASX/US/crypto)
body:
O.P.
Disclosure: I'm the developer of this tool, and it's a paid product.
I wanted to be upfront about that because I'm not here pretending to be an independent user. The reason it's paid is simply that it took around five months to build, I used paid AI tools throughout development, and I continue maintaining and improving it. I built it because I was frustrated with my own setup and now use it every day. If it only ends up helping a handful of people with the same frustrations, that's still a win for me.
The reason I started this thread is to get feedback from Australian investors rather than just promote it.
I was juggling Excel (which I never enjoyed using), plus separate apps for ASX, US shares and crypto. I looked at options like Sharesight and Navexa, but they either didn't fit how I wanted to track everything and are expensive, especially being subscription based to track your investments. Free options are very limited. I wanted something that combined everything in one place, didn't require another subscription, and kept all my data on my own device.
The unusual part is that it's a single HTML file. You open it in any browser, with no installation or account required. It's mobile ready so you don't need to install an app. Your portfolio stays in your browser's local storage. The only internet access is for fetching market prices (Yahoo Finance/CoinGecko) and optional news.
Current features include:
- ASX, US shares and crypto in one portfolio - Unlimited holdings and portfolios - Australian CGT estimates and tax summary - Closed-position profit/loss tracking - Trade analytics - Sector and category breakdowns - Watchlists and price alerts - CSV/JSON import and export - Crypto wallet balance scanner using public addresses
The biggest omissions at the moment are:
- No broker auto-sync (manual entry or CSV import only) - No dividend, franking credit or DRP tracking - CGT calculations are estimates only and shouldn't replace professional tax advice
Those missing features are actually why I'm posting here. I don't personally rely on dividend tracking, so I'd like to understand whether that's the biggest thing stopping Australian investors from moving away from spreadsheets or other portfolio trackers.
For anyone interested in seeing what I'm talking about, there's a free demo with sample data (no signup required): https://folionaire.github.io/Folionaire/
My questions to the community and a few things I'd love feedback on specifically about the app:
- What feature keeps you using your current tracker? - If you still use Excel, what does it do that dedicated apps don't? - If you could change one thing about Sharesight, Navexa or your current setup, what would it be? - The way I have combined ASX, US shares and crypto in one place useful? - Dividend, franking credit and DRP tracking is currently the biggest missing feature, how important would that be for you? - Are CGT estimates, trade history and portfolio analytics features you would actually use? - What feature would you add first if you were using this? - What would you change? - What would make you comfortable replacing Excel or your current tracker with something like this? - Is there anything about the design/approach of the app that you would change?
I plan to continuously improve this to no end, so I'm open to all suggestions, so tell what your most wanted feature would be?
I'd genuinely appreciate the feedback, even if it's critical. The goal is to build something Australian investors actually find useful. I used this for months on end and added everything I wanted, plus lots of unique features and moats.

Very busy, confusing demo that looks like another AI generated app.
That's the feedback I'm here for, but I need one more level of detail to act on it. Which screen felt worst? The dashboard is dense by design: I wanted a true overview, so Portfolio Top Movers (24h) shows all your holdings in one list, whether they're ASX shares, US shares or crypto. I haven't found another tracker that does that with local-only data, which is half of why I built it.
But if it's overwhelming as a first impression, that's a real problem I'd want to fix. Genuine question. I've been using it daily for months, so I appreciate the fresh eyes pointing it out.

TicTacToe writes...
the exact same look and feel as every AI generated app
For what it's worth, the part that took five months wasn't generating code, it was the several hundred rounds of giving direction on the layout, the logo, the information density, and testing it against my real portfolio daily until it worked how I actually invest.
So the look is very much chosen rather than defaulted, but I'll cop that finance dashboards are all visually similar right now, AI or not, websites and emails have the same convergence here. I compared it against most of the portfolio apps out there while building it, and the UI will keep evolving through v1 updates based on exactly this kind of feedback.
The real upside here is how it's built. A lot of people in this space specifically want no account, no login, and no third party holding their data. It's half the reason Portfolio Performance has the following it does. Folionaire's version of that is one readable HTML file. Nearly everything else is an account login, an app install, or your data on someone else's server. Here you can open the source and verify exactly what it does with your data (nothing leaves your browser). That's a claim no closed tracker can make.
If the aesthetics aren't your thing, fair enough, but the demo's now loosened if you want to judge it on function.

The interface is way too busy than a clean interface. Just some basic questions.
The busy interface, you're the second person to say it, so I'm going to take note of it. The dashboard is the densest screen by design (it's the everything at a glance view) but I'm looking at ways to calm that down.
What do you use for API? If my own as indicated, a dummy user wouldn't have known how to do that.
Nothing to set up for a normal user. Prices come built in from Yahoo Finance (shares) and CoinGecko (crypto). You open the file, add holdings, hit fetch, done. The your own API key bit you saw is optional and off by default. If you want richer per-ticker news, you can plug in a free key from a news provider, and power users can route price requests through their own relay for reliability. Both are extras with step-by-step instructions in the app. A dummy user never needs to touch either.
What's the privacy protocol?
There's no account, no login, no analytics and no server of mine. I never see your data, and there is nothing to breach on my end. Your portfolio lives in your browser's local storage on your device, and backups are JSON files you save yourself. To be precise about what does leave your browser is price lookups send ticker symbols only (a request like "price of BHP"), never quantities, values or anything identifying. And because the whole app is one readable HTML file, you don't have to take my word for any of this, the source is right there to check.
Where to go for support if i have an issue with the app?
Email folionaire@outlook.com , and I'll be active in this thread long term. Updates are delivered through your Gumroad library link, and all v1.x updates are included with purchase.
